correctness.rationale: The fixed-rank occupancy probabilities are \(k/n^2\) for one cell and \(k(k-1)/[n^2(n-1)^2]\) for two disjoint cells. Independent Rademacher signs then give exact second and fourth moments. The normalized quartic is \(H_q=T+2qD\) with \(q=3(k-1)/(n-1)^2\). The row-column orthogonal decomposition gives an exact nonnegative lower deficit for \(q<1/(n-1)\), with additive critical equality at \(q=1/(n-1)\). For \(\(q>1\)/(n-1)\), convex interpolation with the full-permutation variance decomposition yields a second exact nonnegative deficit, and its equality forces one equal-magnitude full row or column. The upper bound follows directly for \(q\le1\) and by strictly convex merging of same-row/column masses for \(q>1\) (which occurs only at \((2,2)\) and \((3,3)\)). The continuous quotient attains every intermediate value. Invariant averaging of Euclidean comparison forms proves exact Banach--Mazur distortion; all dimensions n>=2 and ranks 1<=k<=n are addressed. The standalone checker was executed and passed exact independent signed-rook enumeration in 72 cases, endpoint checks n=2..26, and 2380 exact lower deficit checks. Finite checks are only corroboration.

originality.rationale: The primary sources were checked against the theorem: Everitt--Fountain (arXiv:0812.2789, originally 2008-12-15) supplies reflection-monoid background, but full text was unavailable; Malandro (arXiv:1110.5679, first public 2011-10-25) develops rank-stratified rook monoid Fourier/representation analysis, not sharp fourth-moment coefficient norms; Pass and Spektor (arXiv:1412.7859, first public 2014-12-25) optimize pairwise-independent exchangeable ±1 vectors, whereas signed rook entries are zero except on a fixed random matching and do not satisfy their hypotheses. Actual searches for fixed-rank partial signed permutations, rook matrices, sharp L4/L2, one-third rank transition, additive minimizers and precise formula aliases did not reveal a covering theorem. The full matching case alone, which is an existing separate theorem, is strictly a boundary specialization and does not determine the new lower transition or the critical additive family. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent treatment remains.

value.rationale: Uniform rank-k nonattacking rook matrices form natural finite measure spaces interpolating between sparse single-cell sampling and full signed permutation matrices. The result computes sharp norm and Banach--Mazur invariants for the full \(n^2\)-dimensional linear coefficient space at every rank, rather than an arbitrary slice. It discovers the exact rank threshold \(\(n=3k-2\)\), exhibits a large additive nonunique minimizer family at equality, distinguishes flat and row-localized norm geometry on either side, and provides exact nonnegative quantitative deficits. This classification has direct use in sharp comparisons for finite sampling of partial matchings and their coefficient spaces. The full-rank boundary result does not supply the new transition; no general downstream theorem is claimed.
